chapter: Return to New York, addiction, health and the NBC job
title: Why bandleaders avoided addicts, and his press coverage
summary: Leaders feared addiction was catching; the Black press and Ebony covered his arrests.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: You couldn't get any jobs because you were using?
Well, evidently, because a lot of

band leaders had the attitude that it was catching, you know. Like a disease or something, you know. And then you're unreliable. They're looking for you at work and you're out trying to acquire narcotics and you come in late or you don't show up at all because you're too sick.
Or if you get busted the name that gets in the headlines is the bandleader's, not yours.
No, I haven't found that to ring so true.
It happened in a lot of cases.
In all my cases they spelled my name loud and clear. Los Angeles Jet and The Sentinel and what have you. All of Johnson's publications.
Yeah. In fact, in the Ebony Magazine, I forget what issue and what year it was, but they had all the drug addicts in the centerfold of the magazine, The Ebony.
In the entertainment business or just --
